repo.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability
repo.name: neovim

body: This is a part 2 of #34778 (part 1 - #41075). It documents the shape of `manifest.dependencies` and uses it in `:checkhealth vim.pack` to report problems with dependencies. There are also two minor improvements to `:che vim.pack`. The plan is to reach an agreement about the `manifest.dependency` shape, merge this (as this is rather low risk), and re-evaluate if it is reasonable to attempt part 3 (use `manifest.dependencies` to compute `deps` field of the lockfile to improve installation/loading order) before the 0.13 release. --- Here is a sample of how `:che vim.pack` output for not fully conforming setup:

comment_data.body: does the ordering matter, and does the healthcheck enforce it?
Not yet, but it probably will. The dependency order will be preserved in the `deps` field of the lockfile to then install and load dependencies in that exact order.

nested quotes is a bit weird and already implies that parsing is needed, which means we could avoid the nested quotes and just parse version ranges ?

is there precedent for the nested quotes in NPM package.json?

comment_data.body:
> nested quotes is a bit weird and already implies that parsing is needed, which means we could avoid the nested quotes and just parse version ranges ?

The logic is to allow both version ranges (`">=1.0.0"`) and branch/tab/commit (`"'branch'"`) as a single filed. The same as done in `vim.pack.Spec` through `vim.version.range` + string and lockfile through string + quoted string.

I would think that supporting at least branch as potential dependency version is a good thing to have.

Dropping the quotes may result in potential undefined behavior as I would guess there might be tags that look like version ranges. So there needs to be *something* that can separate two cases other than their string content.

> is there precedent for the nested quotes in NPM package.json?

The `package.json` for dependencies has [its own](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json#git-urls-as-dependencies) not ideal way to differentiate `commit-ish` and `semver`, which I'd argue is worse than "nested quotes" (which have precedent in `vim.pack`).

comment_data.body:
> The `package.json` for dependencies has [its own](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json#git-urls-as-dependencies) not ideal way to differentiate `commit-ish` and `semver`, which I'd argue is worse

Yes, and that's the main reason we are diverging from package.json for `dependencies`: its version spec is horrific.

I see that the "quoted string" approach was indicated in https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/49 but I missed it until now. How do other formats approach it? 

Maybe we should distinguish `version` / `tag` / `branch` as separate fields separately to avoid the ambiguity. That's not ideal but I can easily imagine the quoted-string being a constant source of confusion. Quote chars `'` `"` are allowed in git tags so....

Or we could simply not support git tags with version-range characters (`>`, `=`) in them. I think that's reasonable.

comment_data.body:
Full proposal:

- If `< > = ^ ~ * ||` or ASCII whitespace are present in `version`, it is treated as a version/range spec.
    - Git refs with those chars are not supported (SHA is a workaround).
- Else it's treated as a git ref (tag/branch).


| Input | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `1.2.3` | Literal Git ref |
| `v1.2.3` | Literal Git ref |
| `1.2` | Literal Git ref |
| `1.x` | Literal Git ref |
| `main` | Literal Git ref |
| `>=1.2.3` | Semver range |
| `^1.2.3` | Semver range |
| `~1.2.3` | Semver range |
| `1.2.*` | Semver range |
| `>=1.2 <2` | Semver range |
| `1.2.3 \|\| >=2.0.0` | Semver range |

comment_data.body:
> I see that the "quoted string" approach was indicated in [neovim/packspec#49](https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/49) but I missed it until now. How do other formats approach it? Maybe we should support `versionrange` field separately to avoid the ambiguity?

What do you mean by "other formats"?

One approach that is indeed used is to have separate `version`, `branch`, `tag`, `commit` fields to separate them. To me separate manifest/spec fields should indicate independent or "composable" data. Having mutually exclusive fields is a stronger issue to me than allowing `"'branch'"` to mean branch/tag/commit named `branch`.

With two fields `versionrange` and `<something>` (not even sure what is the proper name here would be other than `commit-ish`) there would probably me more confusion as to when to use each one and what happens if both are supplied.

> That's not ideal but I can easily imagine the quoted-string being a constant source of confusion.

I don't think it will be *that* problematic. The scope of affected people is plugin authors (not all users). Among those, the problem will be only for authors who want to limit dependency to a fixed branch/commit/tag. The result is not many, but still non-zero to still support this. 

> Quote chars `'` `"` are allowed in git tags so....

That is not a problem: `version = "''tag'with\"quotes''"`. The only thing that is needed is that the string starts and ends with `'` to indicate that it is branch/tag/commit.

> Full proposal:
> 
>     * If `< > = ^ ~ * ||` or ASCII whitespace are present in `version`, it is treated as a version/range spec.
>       
>       * Git refs with those chars are not supported (SHA is a workaround).
> 
>     * Else it's treated as a git ref (tag/branch).

I don't think this is a good idea to intentionally deny support for some edge cases, **if** there is already a working solution and it is aligned with what is already done in `vim.pack`.

If anything, special casing an manually selected set of ASCII characters is more confusing:
- It takes more effort to describe in the doc.
- Leaves out edge cases.
- Doesn't align with either `vim.pack.Spec` or `vim.version.range()`.

Besides, I can easily see the possibility of reasonable branch names that contain `=` or `~` in them.

> o me separate manifest/spec fields should indicate independent or "composable" data. Having mutually exclusive fields is a stronger issue to me than allowing `"'branch'"`

+1. So we just shouldn't support git refs which the forbidden chars (see previous comment).



> not a problem: `version = "''tag'with\"quotes''"`

If we're going to support that kind of quoting then it is just as reasonable to say that if a git ref contains `< > = ^ ~ * ||` then it needs to be escaped or quoted somehow. So the common case is sane. And we don't even need to support this at all initially, it's forward-compatible if we also disallow quote chars or `\` and track it as a backlog item in https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues . 

If this is acceptable then I'll create a backlog issue.

title: pack: implement packspec support, part 2 (`manifest.dependencies` in `:checkhealth`)
